name: EMA-ribbon trend ride (fast/slow cross above tendence) (Pine import)
rationale: Faithful import of the EMA-ribbon trend strategy (Alorse 'Trend EMA + RSI [Alorse]' EMA 10/20/100 and the '3 EMA/SMA + Cross' trend pattern): go long when a fast EMA crosses above a slow EMA WHILE both sit above a long 'tendence' EMA, ride the trend, and exit when RSI runs hot or after a fixed number of bars in profit. Economic mechanism: a stacked, rising EMA ribbon (fast > slow > long) is the textbook signature of an intact uptrend whose momentum is accelerating — the fast-over-slow cross times the re-acceleration, and the above-tendence condition ensures the cross happens INSIDE a structural uptrend rather than as a dead-cat bounce in a downtrend. Riding it harvests trend persistence; exiting on an overbought RSI or a bars-in-trade cap takes profit before the ribbon rolls over. The distinct structural piece vs our other trend specs: the long 'tendence' EMA is encoded as the MaTrendFilter regime gate (setup.ma_trend_filter, fitted ma_lookback ~100-200), and the fast/slow cross is encoded as positive medium-term momentum (ret_Nd>floor) on a SHORT fitted lookback — a momentum-continuation entry gated by a slow-MA regime, which no existing spec combines this way. Translation losses (noted, not fabricated): (1) the two-EMA crossover event is approximated by ret_Nd>floor on a short lookback (price advancing = fast pulling above slow) rather than a literal crossover of two EMA series, which the registry does not expose as a pair — the Finder fits the lookback to the intended 10/20 window; (2) the 'close > open' single-bar confirmation is dropped (a 1-bar candle filter is noise at the daily/4h horizon, not the edge); (3) the literal EMA periods 10/20/100 become fitted lookbacks (no magic numbers); (4) Alorse's stop = lowest-low over 2x-crossBack bars becomes a fitted stop fraction. Honest prior: EMA-ribbon/golden-cross trend systems are the most common retail trend template; net of ~20bps on crypto spot they typically reduce to fee-eaten momentum — expected a powered fail that maps the trend surface; the Gate disposes. Disconfirmer: the RSI-overbought signal exit takes profit at exhaustion; the time-stop closes a stalled trend; a sub-floor return means the cross failed and the stop bounds it.
catalyst: fast EMA crosses above slow EMA while both hold above the long tendence EMA (ribbon stacked up)
